decisions.reason: The study tested five non-HLA candidate genes across four loci (CCDC122-LACC1, NOD2, TNFSF15, and RIPK2) from the original Chinese GWAS (Zhang et al., 2009), replicating the associations at NOD2 and CCDC122-LACC1 while failing to validate TNFSF15 and RIPK2, so the replication outcome is mixed rather than successful. Parent primary-source confirmation: The original-specific design tests all four Chinese-GWAS non-HLA loci, not merely the two highlighted in the abstract title. Results report23of28tested markers unassociated and identify significant NOD2/CCDC122-LACC1 markers, with Discussion confirming those loci and retaining nonvalidated-gene limitations. This supports partial/mixed validation of the earlier multi-locus finding, not wholesale success or failure of all Chinese findings. Tag SNPs/new associated markers and Brazilian internal follow-up samples are not confused with separate original papers.

parent_primary_scope_evidence.quote:
A second consistent association signal was observed for
rs4942254, which is located intragenic to CCDC122; however extensive LD pattern does not allow excluding neighboring gene LACC1 as the true responsible for the association detected. Finally, a combined plot was conducted to
summarize the information from all samples of the present
study. The results confirmed the host resistance effect for
both loci.

prior_decision.quote: Also, in the present study, it is important to consider that the small sample size of the discovery sample could have an impact upon the power to capture more subtle genetic association effects. Finally, we cannot exclude the possibility that genes not validated/replicated for leprosy per se susceptibility are actually controlling susceptibility to endophenotype of the disease, such as clinical forms and the occurrence of reversal reactions.
